pages.name: index
pages.prompt:
Create a Vue 3 single-page landing experience for 'SpiderNetOS - Agent-Native Operating System'. This is NOT a traditional SaaS landing page. It uses behavioral psychology principles: Framing Effect, Peak-End Rule, and Curiosity Gap Theory.

STRUCTURE:
1. HERO (0-3s): Full-screen dark background with animated particle network (canvas/WebGL). Center text: 'What if your business didn't scale linearly—but autonomously?' No navigation menu visible. Only a subtle pulsing indicator suggesting scroll.

2. REALITY PATHS (3-30s): Three large interactive zones appearing on scroll:
   - BUILD: 'Create an AI-driven system' → opens mini-simulation showing agent swarm
   - SELL: 'Automate revenue generation' → shows revenue curve animation
   - SCALE: 'Deploy autonomous operations' → shows infrastructure graph
   Each zone has parallax depth, hover-triggered glow effects (orange #FF6B2C), and clicking reveals an interactive narrative module (not a new page).

3. PROOF SECTION: Animated metrics that count up - '2.4M agents deployed', '$840M revenue automated', '99.97% uptime'. Use intersection observer to trigger.

4. CONVERSION EMERGENCE: Instead of 'Sign Up', show 'Run Your First System Simulation' as a CTA. Clicking opens an inline terminal-style demo (mock data) showing an agent executing a business task.

5. FOOTER: Minimal. Links to docs, GitHub, status page.

INTERACTION RULES:
- No traditional navbar - navigation is scroll-driven
- Every interactive element has hover feedback (scale 1.02, orange glow box-shadow)
- Scroll hijacking is FORBIDDEN - use natural scroll with GSAP ScrollTrigger
- Mobile: stacked single-column, touch-friendly zones

STYLING:
- Use Tailwind CSS with custom config
- Dark mode only (#0A0A0F background)
- Orange accent (#FF6B2C) for all interactive elements
- Glassmorphism cards: backdrop-blur(12px), bg-white/5, border-white/10
- All animations use transform and opacity (GPU-accelerated)

TECHNICAL:
- Vue 3 Composition API with <script setup>
- GSAP + ScrollTrigger for scroll animations
- Canvas 2D particle network in hero (self-contained component)
- Responsive: breakpoints at 640px, 1024px, 1280px
- No external images - use CSS gradients, SVG icons, and canvas graphics

Generate the COMPLETE App.vue file with all sections as sub-components defined in the same file or as separate component imports.

pages.name: Dashboard
pages.prompt:
Create a customer-facing Dashboard for SpiderNetOS Cockpit. This is where users SEE and CONTROL their autonomous business systems.

CORE PRINCIPLE: The dashboard should feel ALIVE. Users must feel they are observing a living economic organism, not configuring software.

LAYOUT:
- Top bar: Logo, tenant name, notification bell, user avatar, budget indicator (green/yellow/red)
- Left sidebar: Dashboard, Agents, Flows, Approvals, Traces, Usage, Memory, Settings
- Main area: Cards arranged in Bento-grid style

WIDGETS (each is a card):
1. SYSTEM STATE (top-left, 2x2):
   - Live count of active agents (pulsing green dot)
   - Revenue stream visualization (sparkline chart)
   - Active workflows count with trend indicator
   - Opportunities detected this hour

2. AGENT SWARM (top-right, 2x2):
   - Visual representation of running agents as dots/nodes
   - Each agent has status color (green=running, yellow=waiting, red=error)
   - Click to expand agent details

3. REVENUE GRAPH (bottom, full width):
   - Line chart showing revenue over time (last 7 days)
   - Overlay showing agent-contributed vs manual revenue
   - Chart.js or D3 line chart with orange gradient fill

4. QUICK ACTIONS (bottom-right):
   - 'Approve Pending' button with count badge
   - 'Deploy Agent' button
   - 'View Traces' button

5. RECENT EVENTS (sidebar or bottom):
   - Scrollable list of recent agent actions
   - Format: 'AtlasAgent processed query → $0.002'
   - Timestamp, agent name, status icon

INTERACTION:
- All data starts as mock/demo but structured for real API integration
- Cards have hover: subtle lift (translateY -2px), shadow increase
- Clicking any metric opens detail drawer (slide from right)
- Budget indicator pulses red when >90%

STYLING:
- Dark theme (#0F0F14 background)
- Cards: #1A1A24 background, 1px border rgba(255,255,255,0.08), border-radius 12px
- Orange accents for primary actions and active states
- Success green (#00E5C8) for positive metrics
- Monospace font for all numbers/data (JetBrains Mono)

Generate Dashboard.vue with all widgets as inline components or imports. Use Pinia store for state.

pages.name: AgentBuilder
pages.prompt:
Create an Agent Builder interface for SpiderNetOS customers. Users create AI agents by describing what they want in natural language, and the system generates the agent configuration.

LAYOUT:
- Split view: Left = agent canvas/visualization, Right = configuration panel

LEFT PANEL (Agent Canvas):
- Central node representing the agent being built
- Connected nodes showing: Trigger, Action, Memory, Output
- Drag-and-drop connections (visual only, mock)
- Animated data flow particles along connections

RIGHT PANEL (Configuration):
- Name input with auto-suggest
- Description textarea (this is the KEY input - users describe in plain English what the agent should do)
- Capability tags (multi-select chips): Sales, Support, Research, Code, Design, Data
- Automation level slider: 0 (human-in-loop) to 100 (fully autonomous)
- Cost ceiling input ($/day)
- 'Generate Agent' button (primary, orange)

BELOW CONFIG:
- Preview section showing estimated: response time, cost/agent, success probability
- These update live as user types

STYLING:
- Dark theme matching dashboard
- Canvas background: subtle grid pattern
- Nodes: rounded rectangles, colored by type (trigger=orange, action=blue, memory=purple, output=green)
- Connections: animated dashed lines with flowing particles

Generate AgentBuilder.vue with mock data.

- Cost estimate: '$0.45 compute'

FILTER BAR:

- Filter by: Risk level, Agent type, Time range
- Sort by: Urgency, Cost, Time

APPROVED/REJECTED TABS:
- Same card format but with outcome badge
- Show who approved/rejected and when

STYLING:
- Cards have left border colored by status (pending=orange, approved=green, rejected=red)
- Hover reveals quick-approve buttons
- Bulk select checkbox for batch approval

pages.name: SystemObservability
pages.prompt:
Create the SpiderNetOS Internal Observability Dashboard. This is the GOD LAYER for the SpiderNetOS team to observe the entire platform. Think NASA mission control meets cyberpunk UI.

PRINCIPLE: Every pixel must convey system state. No decorative elements. Information density is paramount.

LAYOUT (3-column grid):

COLUMN 1 (Left, 25%):
1. PLATFORM HEALTH (top):
   - Vertical list of all services: Inference, Atlas API, Intelligence, CPL, WebSocket, Nginx
   - Each service: name, status dot (green/yellow/red), latency (ms), uptime %
   - Click to expand recent logs (last 5 lines)

2. GPU CLUSTER (middle):
   - For each GPU (2x RTX 5090):
     - Utilization bar (horizontal, animated)
     - VRAM: used/total with visual bar
     - Temperature: numeric + color (green<75, yellow 75-85, red>85)
     - Power draw in Watts
     - Process list: which agent is using it
   - Real-time updates every 2 seconds (WebSocket data)

3. COST GOVERNOR (bottom):
   - Today's spend: $X.XX / $XX.XX budget
   - Progress bar with color zones
   - Per-tenant cost breakdown (top 5)
   - Alert if any tenant exceeds 80% budget

COLUMN 2 (Center, 50%):
1. AGENT SWARM VISUALIZATION (top, 60%):
   - Force-directed graph of all active agents
   - Nodes: agents (colored by type: Atlas=orange, Forge=blue, Sentinel=red, Prism=purple, Nexus=green)
   - Edges: communication flow between agents
   - Node size = compute usage
   - Edge thickness = message frequency
   - Click node to see agent details panel
   - Real-time layout updates (D3 force simulation or similar)

2. EVENT STREAM (bottom, 40%):
   - Scrolling log of system events
   - Format: [timestamp] [agent] [action] [status] [cost]
   - Color-coded by status (green=success, yellow=warning, red=error)
   - Auto-scroll with pause on hover
   - Filter: All, Errors, High Cost, Agent-specific

COLUMN 3 (Right, 25%):
1. CPL REWARD HEATMAP (top):
   - 3D-style visualization (or 2D heatmap) showing:
     - X: Novelty score
     - Y: Emotional score
     - Color intensity: Utility score
   - Pareto frontier line overlaid
   - Latest scores animate in from edge
   - Historical trail (last 50 scores fade out)

2. EXPLORATION vs EXPLOITATION (middle):
   - Pie chart or gauge showing current ratio
   - Target: 20% explore, 80% exploit (adjustable)
   - Current actual ratio with deviation indicator

3. SYSTEM THROUGHPUT (bottom):
   - Requests/minute sparkline
   - Agent executions/minute
   - Average response time (ms)
   - All with 5-minute trailing window

INTERACTION:
- Everything updates in real-time via WebSocket
- Click any metric to open detailed view (modal or slide-over)
- Keyboard shortcuts: 'g' for GPU focus, 'a' for agents, 'e' for events
- Dark mode only, no theme toggle

STYLING:
- Background: #0A0A0F with subtle grid pattern
- Panels: #12121A background, 1px border rgba(255,255,255,0.06), border-radius 8px
- All data in JetBrains Mono font
- Orange (#FF6B2C) for primary actions and highlights
- Teal (#00E5C8) for positive/success metrics
- Purple (#B967FF) for CPL/RL related elements
- No rounded corners on data elements (sharp, technical feel)
- Minimal padding (information density)

Generate Observability.vue with all panels as components. Include WebSocket connection setup.

pages.name: RLTraining
pages.prompt:
Create a Reinforcement Learning Training view for SpiderNetOS internal team. This shows the CPL (Curiosity-Priority Learning) engine training in real-time.

LAYOUT:

TOP BAR:
- Training status: Running / Paused / Completed
- Episode count, total steps, elapsed time
- Current policy network: architecture summary
- GPU allocation: which GPU is training

MAIN AREA (split):

LEFT (60%):
1. REWARD CURVE (top):
   - Line chart: Episode vs Cumulative Reward
   - Smoothed curve with raw data faint behind
   - Vertical markers for policy updates
   - D3 or Chart.js, orange line on dark background

2. PARETO FRONT (middle):
   - 3D scatter plot (or 2D projection) of multi-objective rewards
   - Axes: Novelty, Emotional Impact, Utility
   - Each point is an episode
   - Pareto frontier highlighted as connected line
   - Color gradient from old (faint) to new (bright)

3. LOSS DECOMPOSITION (bottom):
   - Stacked area chart: Policy loss, Value loss, Entropy loss
   - Shows training stability

RIGHT (40%):
1. HYPERPARAMETERS:
   - Learning rate (slider + numeric)
   - Batch size
   - Discount factor (gamma)
   - GAE lambda
   - Entropy coefficient
   - All editable with immediate effect (if backend connected, else mock)

2. ACTION DISTRIBUTION:
   - Bar chart showing frequency of each action type
   - Actions: deploy, modify, pause, query, explore, exploit
   - Updates per episode

3. AGENT PERFORMANCE TABLE:
   - List of agents with their learned policies
   - Columns: Agent, Win Rate, Avg Reward, Preference Drift, Last Updated
   - Sortable

BOTTOM BAR:
- Control buttons: Start Training, Pause, Save Checkpoint, Load Checkpoint, Reset
- Checkpoint history dropdown

STYLING:
- Technical/scientific aesthetic
- Grid lines on all charts (rgba(255,255,255,0.03))
- Chart lines: orange for primary, teal for secondary, purple for tertiary
- All numeric values monospace
- Buttons: sharp corners, orange border on primary action

Generate RLTraining.vue with mock training data that simulates realistic RL curves.

shared_components.name: WebSocketClient
shared_components.prompt:
Create a robust WebSocket client service for Vue 3/Pinia.

REQUIREMENTS:
- Auto-connect on app mount
- Exponential backoff reconnect (1s, 2s, 4s, 8s, max 30s)
- Heartbeat/ping-pong every 30 seconds
- Message routing by type to Pinia stores
- Connection status indicator
- Graceful handling of server disconnect
- Support both ws:// and wss:// based on window.location.protocol
- Dynamic URL: ws://{hostname}:8002/ws

MESSAGE TYPES TO HANDLE:
- 'gpu': { data: [{id, util, mem_used, mem_total, temp, power, name}] } → systemStore.setGpu()
- 'event': { data: {id, agent, status, intent, cost} } → systemStore.addEvent()
- 'cpl_score': { data: {event_id, novelty, emotional, utility, pareto_distance} } → cplStore.addScore()
- 'service_status': { data: {name, status, latency} } → systemStore.updateService()
- 'telemetry': { data: {...} } → forward to analytics

EXPORT: initWebSocket(), closeWebSocket(), sendMessage(data), getConnectionStatus()

Generate as a plain JavaScript module (not TS).
